conflicts.fact: Charge sign of the cloud and induced charge on the iron roof
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 draws a positive cluster at the cloud base with induced negative charge on the roof's upper surface. Lesson 4 has a negative cloud with positive induced charge on the roof's upper surface. Lesson 5 gives the cloud as -40 C at its base.

conflicts.fact: Charge/energy values for the storm cloud and the cloud-roof distance
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3 gives a cloud with 20 C charge separation 800 m above the roof. Lesson 5 gives up to -40 C at the cloud base. Lesson 7 gives the stored energy as 1.5×10^9 J with a voltage of 300 MV. Lesson 8 attributes the 1.5×10^9 J figure to Lesson 5, which never computes it, and sets up an estimate from current and duration data.

conflicts.fact: Whether Lesson 3 follows Lesson 2's induction content, and the anchoring-phenomenon explanation of the roof
conflicts.versions: Lesson 3's DQB teacher script says 'In Lesson 2 we said the roof gained charge by induction', but induction is only taught in Lesson 4. Lesson 2 instead explains the hairs standing on end by attraction to opposite charges and treats the roof as a conductor pathway.

conflicts.fact: Lesson sequence duplication and the order of Coulomb's Law versus capacitance/Q-V content
conflicts.versions: Lessons 3 and 5 both teach Coulomb's Law as new, with different data sets (torsion balance with Q=3.0e-8 C versus PhET with 1 μC). Lesson 8 says Q-V graph knowledge came from 'Lesson 5 and 6', and its Ol Kalou energy is attributed to Lesson 5, whereas Lesson 5 is Coulomb's Law and the energy comes in Lesson 7.

conflicts.fact: Which capacitor plates/charges the cloud and roof represent
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 labels the cloud base the negative plate and the roof the positive plate, with air as dielectric. Lesson 7 describes the cloud-to-ground gap as the capacitor. Lesson 3 has a positive cloud base.

conflicts.fact: Why the lightning conductor/iron roof was struck
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the iron roof was struck because, as a conductor, it concentrates charge and provides a low-resistance path. Lesson 5 says it was the closest large conductor, maximising F, and that the conductor's height minimised r. Lesson 9 attributes it to field concentration at the pointed tip.

conflicts.fact: Duration of the Ol Kalou-based Lesson 9 summative task
conflicts.versions: Lesson 9 model phase says 8 minutes, while the teacher script says 'seven full minutes of silence'.
Lesson 6 says the foil capacitor stores about 200 to 500 picofarads. Lesson 8 uses the Lesson 6 foil capacitor as C = 470 microfarads (about a million times larger), giving 19 mJ at 9 V.
